question.text: It has been found that for a chemical reaction with rise in temperature by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>9</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math> the rate constant gets doubled. Assuming a reaction to be occurring at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>300</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math>, the value of activation energy is found to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>kJmol</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. [nearest integer] (Given <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>ln</mi><mn>10</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>mol</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>30</mn></math>)

solution.text:
Arrhenius equation for the rate constant of a reaction in terms of energy of activation at two different temperatures is given by

logK2K1=Ea2.3R1T1-1T2

Rise in temperature =9 K

Initial temperature =300 K

logK309K300=Ea2.3R1300-1309

log2=Ea2.3R9300×309

Ea=2.3×0.30×300×3099

Ea=58.988×103 J=58.988kJ=59kJ
